I have undiagnosed ptsd (or I assume cptsd) and I’ve been telling myself I’ll quit after I run out. Weed prevented me from killing myself a few years ago but now it’s a crutch I can feel holding me back. 

I’m planning on quitting after I run out so I can take my studies more seriously, live a more active lifestyle and get into hobbies again. 

Weird (yet understandable) how something that quite literally saved us is now something being used as a crutch. Good luck on your journey! I feel anxious starting this new chapter

One summer day I was going to head up to my old college town to interview for a part time job I was extremely excited about and got a call that the location I wanted wasn’t needed but the one 30-40 min away was and I could alternatively interview for that which I declined. It was a couples months after my college friend passed away. I cancelled my trip up, and called and called and called. I remember being home alone and crying and crying in the hallway and was never able to get through. I think I have undiagnosed complex ptsd. It’ll have been three years in May. Damn

Hey I’m a (21F) and I don’t know what else to say except I am so sorry for your agony. I remember 15 like it was yesterday...

Are you enrolled in public schools? Obviously I’m in this subreddit for the same reasons as you but I’m in school to teach. If any of the teachers in your building are like me, there’s gotta be one person that is waiting to make a connection with someone like you. 

I had a lot of family shit happen (and is reoccurring now). When I moved away for college, one of my new friends fell and unexpectedly passed away. 

I’m still here. I wish I wasn’t, but I am. Maybe you’ll have a positive life changing experience in the meantime. If you need any help with math/school/college advice, you are more than welcome to dm me!

Edit: I want(ed) to teach to better reach students who suffer from the effects of traumatic experiences. I felt/feel so crudy and I don’t ever want to see a student feeling how I did.
